inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market: director-only restricted stock / stock options; share acquisition rights balance JPY 4.0bn at 2026-09-30 (H1 FY2026 presentation p.7). No cash-flow SBC line is disclosed in the integrated report or presentations; charge treated as nil (<0.05% of revenue).
inputs.buyback_note: JPY 350bn buyback executed May 2026 (H1 FY2026 presentation p.32), ~5% of shares; the share count below is post-buyback, so the buyback is already in the divisor and is NOT a recurring flow in the model. Management says JPY 700bn is 'not an upper limit' but future buybacks are discretionary and not modelled.
inputs.share_count_basis: 278.2m = FY2026 forecast profit attributable to owners (JPY 280.0bn) / forecast EPS (JPY 1,006.45), H1 FY2026 presentation p.32, i.e. the company's own post-buyback count (292.8m before the May-2026 buyback). Held FLAT: no SBC to dilute and no non-SBC issuance planned. Share acquisition rights (JPY 4.0bn) are immaterial dilution.
inputs.fy0: FY2025 (Daikin label; year ended 31 March 2026 = CSV row FY2026)
inputs.fiscal_label_note: Daikin labels its fiscal year by the April start (FY2025 = Apr-2025 to Mar-2026). The Metrics CSV labels by the March end (FY2026). Year 1 of the projection is Daikin FY2026 = year ending 31 March 2027, the current guidance year.
inputs.net_debt_note: Interest-bearing debt JPY 1,330.3bn at 2026-09-30 (short-term borrowings 302.4 + CP 158.6 + bonds 295.0 + long-term borrowings 369.0 + lease debt 205.3) less cash and deposits 932.0 = net debt 398.3bn. Debt rose 282bn YoY to part-fund the buyback. Non-controlling interests (JPY 61.2bn book) are NOT deducted here; NCI leakage is charged in the flows via the cash_tax_rate_path (see nci_treatment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-denominated flows discounted at a JPY-built WACC of 7.5% for all three scenarios. Build: 10y JGB ~1.8% risk-free, 5.5% equity risk premium, beta ~1.0 for a global cyclical industrial -> cost of equity ~7.3%; after-tax cost of debt ~1%; market-value weights ~82/18 give a CAPM WACC near 6.2%. 7.5% is used deliberately as the house rate for a cyclical, tariff-exposed industrial (house reference 9% is for small keiretsu suppliers; Daikin is a JPY 6tn global leader). Risk is charged ONCE: cyclicality, tariffs, Chinese price competition and FUSION 30 execution live in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario WACC premiums.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease debt JPY 205.3bn is inside total_debt / net debt; no lease principal is deducted from the flows. Daikin is a J-GAAP filer; the lease debt is largely overseas subsidiaries' IFRS 16 / ASC 842 liabilities consolidated into interest-bearing debt. Their right-of-use depreciation sits inside D&A and their renewal is not in capex; this is offset in the build by ~JPY 51bn/yr of goodwill and intangible amortisation (D&A 276.2 vs PP&E depreciation 224.8 in FY2025) which also needs no replacement capex. Terminal D&A% (5.0) is held BELOW terminal capex% (5.3) so the add-back cannot exceed reinvestment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: profit attributable to non-controlling interests runs ~JPY 11-12bn/yr (H1 FY2025 5.9bn, H1 FY2026 5.5bn), ~2.5pp of pre-tax profit. cash_tax_rate_path = 29.0% effective tax burden (FY2025 29.7%, H1 FY2026 29.0%) + 2.5pp NCI leakage = 31.5%. The NCI stock (JPY 61.2bn) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. Tie-out: FY2025 OP 415.0 x (1-0.315) = 284 vs attributable net profit 275.2 after a 23.6bn non-operating loss in H2 and 20.1bn interest income outside OP.
inputs.excluded_income_note: The flows are built from EBITDA = operating profit + D&A, so interest income (JPY 20.1bn FY2025) and dividend income on cross-shareholdings are already outside the flows. Matching-asset rule: cash is in net debt and investment securities (JPY 201.2bn at 2026-09-30, mostly listed cross-shareholdings) are added in equity_bridge. Owner FCF (last_fcf) strips interest income from the reported FCF so the historical base is consistent.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials'), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: JPY WACC, treatment (A) leases, NCI as leakage in the flows, matching-asset bridge for investment securities, SBC-zero (house and street coincide, band_position null). Reported FCF (FY2025) = OCF 465.8 - capex 300.0 = 165.8bn; owner FCF = 165.8 - 0 SBC - 20.1 interest income = 145.7bn (2.9% of revenue). Year-1 owner FCF margin in the base build is ~4.2%, above FY2025, because (i) capex steps down from the FY2024 peak 324.6 -> 300.0 -> FY2026 plan 285.0 and (ii) FY2025 working capital consumed ~41% of incremental revenue versus the 5-year average of ~24% (inventory days already down from 82 to 73 at Sep-2026). Price is the Yahoo Finance regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 17,380-26,440. Fresh build, no prior DCF.
inputs.units_note: All money fields are millions of JPY (e.g. base_revenue 5,015,036 = JPY 5,015.0bn). Prose notes quote billions for readability.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 presentation balance sheet, 2026-09-30. Added because their dividend income is outside the EBITDA-based flows (matching-asset rule). Not marked down for the ~25% tax on unrealised gains; immaterial (~JPY 150/share).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-scenario years 1-5 average; not the equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-yr equity CAGR 13.3% vs 3-yr EPS CAGR 2.2%: equity growth is retained earnings plus yen-depreciation translation gains on an 84%-overseas asset base, while EPS stalled on margin compression (OP margin 9.5% -> 8.3%). Neither is an organic revenue path; the 5-yr revenue CAGR of 15% includes the FY2022-23 post-COVID catch-up and yen weakness.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs to Daikin FY2025 (Mar-2026) from FY2022 (Mar-2023) and FY2020 (Mar-2021), 11-year summary in the FY2025 integrated report. Owner FCF = company-defined FCF (OCF + investing CF) less interest income: Mar-2021 204.3bn -> Mar-2023 -70.9bn (capex and inventory build) -> Mar-2026 123.5bn. The 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (negative base); the 5-yr CAGR is -9.6% against a +15% revenue CAGR, which is the FUSION 25 capex supercycle (capex/OCF 58%) and inventory build that FUSION 30 is explicitly targeting (capex/OCF 43%).

base.growth_note: Y1 = FY2026 guidance raised 2026-11-05 to net sales JPY 5,440bn (+8.5%), of which ~JPY 125bn (2.5pp) is FX. Thereafter decelerating from 6% toward 2.5%, in line with FUSION 30's structural drivers (data-centre Applied, IMEA, Solutions mix) but below the 15% 5-yr CAGR which was inflated by yen weakness and the post-COVID catch-up.
base.margin_note: EBITDA margin = OP margin + D&A%. OP margin 8.4% in Y1 (guidance JPY 455bn), rising 0.4pp/yr to 10.0% in Y5 and plateauing at 10.5%. This is a deliberate haircut: FUSION 30 targets 10% by FY2028 (Y3) and 12%+ by FY2030 (Y5), but FUSION 25 targeted 11% and delivered 8.3%.
base.capex_note: FY2026 plan JPY 285bn = 5.2% of guided revenue; held at 5.3% thereafter, above the FUSION 30 capex/OCF 43% target (~4.5% of revenue) to fund Saudi/India/data-centre capacity. D&A 5.5% (FY2025 actual 276.2/5,015) drifting to 5.0% as goodwill amortisation runs off.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: receivables 1,026 + inventories 1,164 vs payables 454 at Sep-2026, so growth consumes cash. -24% capture of incremental revenue is the FY2021-FY2025 cumulative average (EBITDA less tax paid minus OCF, over the revenue increase); FY2025 alone was -41%.
base.tax_note: 29.0% effective tax burden + 2.5pp NCI leakage; see inputs.nci_treatment.
base.terminal_note: WACC 7.5% / g 2.0% gives Gordon ~18.5x; cap 18x binds. 18x owner FCF for a mature global HVAC leader is below the current ~22x P/E and below Carrier/Trane multiples.

bull.margin_note: FUSION 30 delivered on schedule: OP margin 10.0% in FY2028 (Y3) and 12.0% in FY2030 (Y5), plateau 12.5%; capex/OCF falls toward the 43% target; inventory days keep falling so WC drag eases to -20%.

bear.margin_note: FUSION 30 repeats FUSION 25: OP margin stuck at 7.6-8.3% as tariffs, raw materials and Chinese price competition absorb the mix gains; FY2027 revenue flat as the FX tailwind reverses and US residential stays rate-constrained; capex stays near 5.5% to defend share; terminal cap 15x for a cyclical that has not re-rated.

scenario_narratives.base: Daikin grows revenue 8.5% in the guidance year (about a third of it FX) and then 5-6% a year as data-centre Applied cooling, IMEA capacity (Sri City, Saudi plant) and the Solutions mix shift (28% -> 40% of AC sales) offset a soft China and a rate-constrained US residential market. Operating margin improves ~0.4pp a year from 8.4% to 10% by FY2030 and plateaus at 10.5%: real progress on FUSION 30's cost and mix programme, but two years late and 1.5pp short of the 12% target, consistent with FUSION 25's record. Capex steps down from the FY2024 peak and working capital keeps consuming about a quarter of incremental revenue. Terminal value is bound by the 18x cap, so the base case does not rely on a re-rating.
scenario_narratives.bull: FUSION 30 is delivered on schedule under Elliott's scrutiny: operating margin reaches 10% in FY2028 and 12% in FY2030, with the Solutions business supplying ~70% of AC gross-profit growth and the Chemicals segment (FEP for data-centre cabling, semiconductor materials) compounding at 14%+ sales growth on 14% margins. Revenue compounds 7-9% through FY2030 as data-centre cooling triples in North America and India/Middle East grow double digits. Capex discipline (capex/OCF 43%) and falling inventory days lift FCF conversion; a 20x terminal multiple reflects a company that has closed the margin gap to Carrier and Trane. Further buybacks beyond the modelled flat count would be upside not captured here.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FX tailwind reverses, US tariffs and the HVAC price-fixing class action weigh on North America, Chinese price competition caps pricing in China/ASEAN and European heat-pump demand stays weak, so revenue stalls in FY2027 and grows only 2-3% thereafter. Operating margin slips below 8% and never recovers above 8.3%, FUSION 30 missing its targets exactly as FUSION 25 did. Capex stays elevated to defend share while working capital keeps absorbing cash; the debt taken on for the buyback (equity ratio 55.5% -> 51.0%) narrows the balance-sheet buffer. The terminal multiple compresses to 15x for a cyclical industrial with no margin story.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% and bull cut from 35% to 25%. The bull case requires FUSION 30 to hit margin targets that the identical-looking FUSION 25 missed by 2.7pp, while the bear axes (US tariffs already forced a Feb-2026 guidance cut, an open antitrust class action, Chinese price competition, a debt-funded buyback) are live rather than hypothetical. No going-concern or covenant risk, so bear is not pushed higher. Weights sum to 1.0.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on EBITDA-derived flows in JPY, discounted at a single 7.5% JPY WACC with risk carried in three probability-weighted scenario paths. The valuation turns on one question: does FUSION 30 lift operating margin from 8.3% toward 10-12%? The base case gives management half credit (10.5% plateau, two years late). Leases are debt, NCI is a 2.5pp leakage in the flows, cross-shareholdings are added in the bridge, SBC is nil so house and street coincide, and the share count is the post-buyback 278.2m held flat.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: each 1pp of terminal OP margin is worth roughly JPY 2,000-2,500/share; FUSION 25 missed by 2.7pp
Working-capital capture: FY2025 consumed 41% of incremental revenue vs the -24% modelled; a return to that rate removes ~JPY 50bn/yr of FCF
US tariffs and the HVAC price-fixing class action (E.D. Mich., March 2026) are unquantified and sit only in the bear weight
FX: ~84% of sales are overseas; the Y1 growth includes ~2.5pp of yen weakness that can reverse
Lease treatment (A) relies on goodwill amortisation offsetting right-of-use depreciation inside D&A; if the amortisation is smaller than ~JPY 50bn the add-back is overstated by up to ~JPY 300/share
Debt-funded buyback: interest-bearing debt up JPY 282bn YoY; further 'flexible' buybacks are not modelled either as cash out or as fewer shares
